caption_en:
Ireland, judged like Israel. Ready? 🇮🇪

Satire. Every "finding" uses the same rules people use on Israel. The true parts are real:

1. Vikings founded Dublin as a settlement in 841 AD.
2. The Constitution of Ireland (1937) opens "In the Name of the Most Holy Trinity". About 88% of primary schools are under Catholic patronage (Department of Education).
3. From 1937 to 1999, Articles 2 and 3 claimed the whole island, Northern Ireland included. Voters changed them in the 1998 referendum.
4. Saint Patrick and the snakes is a legend, and the stamp is pure satire.

Ireland isn't a theocracy. Neither is Israel, where about 21% of citizens are Arab and Arab parties won 19 Knesset seats in October 2026. Both countries have real problems. Judge them by one standard.
caption_he: אירלנד, אם היו שופטים אותה כמו את ישראל. סאטירה: כל "ממצא" משתמש באותם כללים שמפעילים על ישראל. החלקים האמיתיים: הוויקינגים ייסדו את דבלין ב-841. החוקה האירית נפתחת "בשם השילוש הקדוש", וכ-88% מבתי הספר היסודיים בחסות קתולית. במשך 62 שנים החוקה תבעה את כל האי, כולל צפון אירלנד, עד שהבוחרים שינו אותה ב-1998. אירלנד היא לא תאוקרטיה. גם ישראל לא, כשכ-21% מאזרחיה ערבים והמפלגות הערביות זכו ב-19 מושבים בכנסת. לשתי המדינות יש בעיות אמיתיות. אותו סטנדרט לכולן.

lines.line: Official report. Finding one: Dublin is a settlement.
Vikings founded it in 841. Give it back to Norway!
Finding two: a religious state. The constitution opens in the name of the Most Holy Trinity.
Most primary schools? About 88 percent are under Catholic patronage.
Finding three: for 62 years, the constitution claimed the whole island. Northern Ireland included. Voters changed it in 1998.
Finding four: Saint Patrick drove out all the snakes. Not one left. Ethnic cleansing.
Sounds ridiculous? Israel hears it every day.
Ireland isn't a theocracy. Neither is Israel, where one in five citizens is Arab. Both have real problems. One standard.
